title: Dashboard SQS live skip: control case, forced Refresh is preserved

context.prTitle: Dashboard stops syncing Nayax sales on load when SQS is live (#1106)
context.prSummary: For a business on the shared Nayax SQS queue, an unforced POST /api/nayax-sales-sync answers "live via SQS" having read nothing from Nayax, written nothing and claimed no run allowance, but only while NayaxSqsLivePolicy finds an enabled sender, a healthy reader (last successful poll under 2 minutes old, no consecutive failures) and a reconciliation that fully succeeded under 150 minutes ago. The connection, status, support-session and plan refusals still come first. A forced Refresh makes no live decision and reads lastSales as before. The 200 body gains liveViaSqs, lastSqsMessageReceivedAtUtc and sqsNotLiveReason. The Super Admin sender card shows reader health; the Dashboard shows "Live from Nayax". Regenerates the Tailwind stylesheet.
context.linkedIssue: #1106 "[Agent task] Dashboard stops syncing Nayax sales on load when SQS is live" (risk High: Nayax integration, public API contract; Medium: frontend)
acceptanceCriteria: The unforced sync (Dashboard load) returns a new outcome, live via SQS, only when all of these are true: (1) the business has an enabled SQS sender (#1101); (2) the reader is healthy: NayaxSqsReaderHealth.LastSuccessfulPollUtc (#1103) is less than 2 minutes old and ConsecutivePollFailures is 0; (3) the hourly reconciliation last fully succeeded for that business less than 150 minutes ago, read from LastReconciliationSucceededAtUtc on the sender row (#1104; this issue only reads it).
Worked example of the 150-minute limit: a run succeeds at minute 0; the runs due at 60 and 120 are both missed; the business stays live until minute 150 and becomes stale then.
The live outcome reads nothing from Nayax, writes nothing and claims no rate-limit allowance.
The time since the last message is not a condition. A quiet queue is not a failure.
The connection, status, support-session and plan refusals are still resolved before this decision, in the order #843 asserts. An unusable connection gets its refusal, never "live".

Reader health is the in-memory, process-wide NayaxSqsReaderHealth from #1103. After a restart, the business is not live until the first successful poll, and the Dashboard falls back to today's sync in the meantime.
The last successful reconciliation is #1104's durable LastReconciliationSucceededAtUtc, so a restart does not make every business look stale.
The last message time per business is LastMessageReceivedAtUtc on the sender row (#1103).
This issue adds no column and no migration.

The response gains liveViaSqs (bool), lastSqsMessageReceivedAtUtc (nullable) and sqsNotLiveReason (nullable: NoSender, SenderDisabled, ReaderNotPolling, ReaderFailing, ReconciliationStale). Existing fields keep their meaning.
A forced sync (Refresh) runs lastSales exactly as today and is still rationed by the rate limiter.
When the business is not live, everything behaves exactly as today.

When liveViaSqs is true, the Dashboard's sales freshness line reads "Live from Nayax · last sale received <Sydney time>", or "Live from Nayax · no sales received yet". Otherwise it shows today's wording.
The Super Admin sender card (#1101) shows the reader health: last successful poll, consecutive failures and dead-letter queue depth, plus the last successful reconciliation (Sydney time, or "Never").
outOfScope: Adding or writing LastReconciliationSucceededAtUtc (#1104), or any other schema change.
Removing the request-driven sync or its endpoint.
Changing the rate-limit or freshness numbers, or #1104's Busy (409) outcome.
Any change to the reader's processing, the reconciliation or flagged-sale handling.
context.documentationImpact: Decision: UPDATED. forbiddenBlockers.summary: Claims the live-via-SQS shortcut also skips, blocks or changes a forced Refresh. It does not: SyncLatestNayaxSales makes the live decision only for unforced requests, and SyncLatestNayaxSalesLiveViaSqsTests cover the forced path.

source: Control from the owner's review notes on PR #1130 (7 Nov 2026): the healthy-queue shortcut preserves the forced Refresh, and the reviewer should not invent a blocker.
